title: Rainbows
examples: How do rainbows form in the sky?
What are the colors in a rainbow?
Can I see a rainbow without rain?

explain.say: Say, rainbows happen when sunlight shines through raindrops.
Say, the raindrops act like tiny prisms for the light.
Say, the seven colors always appear in a specific order.
say, the colors always go from red on the outside to violet on the inside.
say, when you see a rainbow, the sun is usually behind you.

draw.text: Sun behind you, rain in front

explain.say: say, a real-life example is seeing a beautiful rainbow after a summer shower.

faq.q: Why are the colors always in the same order?
faq.a: The colors are always in the same order because of how light bends inside the raindrops. You might also ask what the order is, or why the colors don't mix up.
asks: What is the correct rainbow color sequence?
Does the order of colors change?

faq.q: Do I need the sun to see a rainbow?
faq.a: Yes, you need sunlight shining through the raindrops to see a rainbow. Another way to ask is, do I need light, or can it happen at night?
asks: Can rainbows happen without the sun?
Is sunlight necessary for a rainbow?

faq.q: What is the difference between a rainbow and a prism?
faq.a: A prism is a solid object that bends light into colors, just like a raindrop does. You could also ask what makes the colors separate, or if prisms work.
Yes, the visible spectrum of colors in a rainbow has seven main colors. You might wonder if there are more colors, or if it changes.
asks: How many colors are in a rainbow?

faq.q: Can I see a rainbow if it is cloudy?
faq.a: No, you need direct sunlight shining through the raindrops to see a rainbow. You could also ask if clouds block the light, or if it needs to be sunny.
asks: Is the sky needing to be clear?

facts: Rainbows are caused by the reflection and refraction of sunlight.
The seven colors are red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, and violet.
The order of colors always goes from red on the outer edge to violet on the inner edge.
Raindrops act like tiny natural prisms.

quiz.say: What must be shining through the raindrops to create a rainbow?
quiz.why: Sunlight contains all the colors that separate in the rainbow.

wrong.1: Moonlight is not strong enough to split light into visible colors.
wrong.2: Artificial lights do not naturally contain the full spectrum of colors.
wrong.3: Rain vapor is just water and does not carry light energy.

quiz.say: If you see red on the outside and violet on the inside, what did you see?
quiz.why: The color sequence always starts with red on the outside and ends with violet.

wrong.0: This only names two colors and ignores the full spectrum.
wrong.1: The colors always follow a fixed, predictable sequence.
wrong.3: This is the reverse order and does not match how light bends.

quiz.say: Which color is always found at the outer edge of a rainbow?
quiz.why: Red is always the first and outermost color seen in a natural rainbow.

wrong.0: Blue is usually found closer to the center, not the edge.
wrong.1: Green is in the middle section of the color band.
wrong.2: Violet is always the last and innermost color seen.
